notes.sol: Directly verified the missing time column in figshare 23578698 Data.zip/KSS_data.csv and its use in the pinned KSS script. C1/C2 report values 0.11/0.05 are noncanonical diagnostics; Table 1 separately calls interaction BF 0.01 matched, an unresolved report inconsistency. C5 no longer substitutes pairwise yellow-bright versus blue-dim BF 0.52 for overall-condition BF 0.62. Primary DLMO and melatonin claims recur; KSS and supplementary outputs have problems, hence computational issues, with computationally reproducible retained as the source-summary interpretation.
notes.claude: C1, C2 and C5 are not_checkable P0: the shipped KSS data lack the 'time' column the script filters on. The report's 0.11/0.05 are diagnostics; its 0.52 is a different contrast (yellow-bright vs blue-dim) and is not a reference for C5. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: The report states 'There was no attempt to make random number generation reproducible (e.g. with the set.seed() function)'. 'Major Deviations in Results: We were unable to replicate ... Supplementary Table 20.' I confirmed directly that KSS_data.csv (figshare 23578698, Data.zip) has columns PB_No, appointment, condition, KSS_value, KSS_no, gender, with no 'time' column, while BlumeC_NHB_KSS.R at the pinned commit filters on time == 'Evening_1'. The report itself is inconsistent for the KSS interaction (text 0.11/0.05 vs Table 1 0.01 'matched'). Paper-level status is 'computational issues' because KSS outputs and Supp Table 20 did not recur, while the primary claim (C3) did.
